newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials fall on cautious sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials fall on cautious sentiment.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares traded mostly weaker on Tuesday on cautious sentiment, with many brokers expecting the market to remain soft ahead of new issues due next month.
"There is some high degree of cautiousness. People are doing their sums, studying the trends and that likely to keep things on the quiet, soft lane," one broker said.
"We may see some greater commitment after the new issues," he added.

On Tuesday, the main industrial index dropped 57.84 points to end at 10,593.11, dragged down largely by bluechips banking group Barclays, which lost 200 cents to 3,400, hotel and supermarkets group Meikles, which traded 150 cents down at 2,700, and clothing retailer Edgars' 's 100-cent loss at 4,900.

But the secondary seven-share mining index posted a 51.51-point rise to 957.52 mainly on the back of 300-cent gains each in gold miners Falcon at 900 and Rio Tinto at 2,300, both winning local investor support on a firm bullion price.

Coal producer Wankie and nickel miners Bindura also gained five cents to 510, and 35 cents to 750 respctively on a mining portfolio which has lately received little investor backing due to generally low mineral prices.
"People are watching the prices and the fundamentals and there is some level of support coming in, but its slow and very calculated," a broker commented.
